title: Cultural Diversity
description: Explores vocabulary and structures for discussing cultural differences, customs and traditions, cross-cultural misunderstandings, and sensitivity in international settings. For A2 completers working or studying in multicultural environments.

content.content: {"time":1700000401000,"blocks":[{"id":"aA1bB2cC3d","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Culture refers to the shared beliefs, values, customs, and social behaviours of a group of people. Being able to talk about your own culture and ask about others' is an important communication skill at B1 level."}},{"id":"dD4eE5fF6g","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Key vocabulary:"}},{"id":"gG7hH8iI9j","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["tradition — a custom that has been practised for a long time","heritage — the cultural practices and values passed down through generations","identity — the sense of who you are, including your cultural background","customs — accepted ways of behaving in a particular society","values — principles or standards that a culture considers important","community — a group of people who share common characteristics or interests"]}},{"id":"jJ0kK1lL2m","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Useful phrases:"}},{"id":"mM3nN4oO5p","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["In my culture, it is common to...","Where I come from, people usually...","One tradition that is very important to us is...","I grew up in a family where..."]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

phrases.text: In my culture, it is common to...
One tradition that is very important to us is...
phrases.translation: Одна традиция, которая очень важна для нас, — это...

phrases.text: I grew up in a family where...
Where I come from, people usually...
phrases.translation: Там, откуда я родом, люди обычно...

content.text: In my culture, it is common to remove your shoes before entering a home.

pairs.right: a long-standing custom passed through generations
cultural practices and values inherited from ancestors
a sense of who you are, including your background
accepted social behaviours in a community
principles a culture considers important

content.text: In my culture, it is [common] to greet elders by kissing their hand as a sign of [respect]. One [tradition] that is very important to us is gathering as a family for Sunday lunch. Our [heritage] includes folk music, traditional dances, and local festivals.

pairs.english: One tradition that is very important to us is celebrating the New Year with family.
pairs.russian: Одна из наших важных традиций — встречать Новый год в кругу семьи.

pairs.english: In my culture, it is common to remove your shoes before entering a home.
pairs.russian: В моей культуре принято снимать обувь перед входом в дом.

pairs.english: I grew up in a family where showing respect for elders was essential.
pairs.russian: Я вырос в семье, где уважение к старшим было обязательным.

content.content: {"time":1700000402000,"blocks":[{"id":"pP6qQ7rR8s","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Comparing cultures requires careful use of language to avoid generalisations and show respect. At B1 level, use comparison structures and softening language."}},{"id":"sS9tT0uU1v","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Comparison structures:"}},{"id":"vV2wW3xX4y","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["In [Country A], people tend to..., whereas in [Country B]...","One difference between ... and ... is that...","Unlike in my country, in Japan it is customary to..."]}},{"id":"yY5zA6bB7c","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Softening language (to avoid stereotypes):"}},{"id":"cC8dD9eE0f","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["In general... / Generally speaking...","Many people in ... tend to...","It is often said that... / There is a perception that...","Of course, this varies from person to person."]}},{"id":"fF1gG2hH3i","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Example: Generally speaking, in Japan there is a strong emphasis on punctuality and social harmony. In contrast, in some Mediterranean cultures, social interactions tend to be more relaxed and flexible. Of course, this varies from person to person."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: Generally speaking, in Japan there is a strong emphasis on punctuality and social harmony.

mistakeItems.correctText: Generally speaking, punctuality is highly valued in Germany.

topics.title: Module 2: Customs and Traditions Around the World

content.content: {"time":1700000403000,"blocks":[{"id":"iI4jJ5kK6l","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Greetings are one of the most visible aspects of culture. They vary greatly between countries and contexts."}},{"id":"lL7mM8nN9o","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Examples of greeting customs around the world:"}},{"id":"oO0pP1qQ2r","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["UK / USA — handshake in formal settings; hug or wave between friends","France — cheek kisses (la bise) — usually two, sometimes four","Japan — bow; the deeper the bow, the more respectful","Middle East — handshake, often holding hands for a moment as a sign of warmth","New Zealand (Maori) — hongi: pressing noses and foreheads together"]}},{"id":"rR3sS4tT5u","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Modal verbs for describing customs:"}},{"id":"uU6vV7wW8x","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["In Japan, you should bow when greeting someone.","You shouldn't use someone's first name unless invited to.","It is considered rude to...","It is expected that you will..."]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: In Japan, you should bow when greeting someone. The deeper the bow, the more respectful.

content.content: {"time":1700000404000,"blocks":[{"id":"xX9yY0zA1b","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Food customs are deeply connected to culture. What is considered polite at the dinner table in one country may be rude in another."}},{"id":"bB2cC3dD4e","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Examples of food customs:"}},{"id":"eE5fF6gG7h","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["Japan — it is considered polite to say itadakimasu before eating; slurping noodles is acceptable and even complimentary","China — leaving a small amount of food on your plate can signal that you are full and satisfied; finishing everything might imply you were not given enough","Middle East / India — eating with your right hand is traditional; the left hand is considered unclean","Turkey — it is common to share dishes rather than order individual meals","UK — placing your cutlery together after eating signals you have finished"]}},{"id":"hH8iI9jJ0k","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Key vocabulary: cutlery, host, portion, to serve, course (starter / main / dessert), to compliment the host, to toast"}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: In many cultures, it is polite to compliment the host on the food they have prepared.

pairs.right: knives, forks, and spoons
the person who invites guests and serves food
to raise a glass and wish good health
the amount of food served to one person
a part of a meal (starter, main, dessert)

content.text: In many Middle Eastern cultures, it is [traditional] to eat with your right hand. In Japan, it is [polite] to say a phrase of gratitude before your meal. In China, leaving a small amount of food on your plate [signals] that you are full and satisfied with the meal.

content.content: {"time":1700000405000,"blocks":[{"id":"kK1lL2mM3n","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Different cultures have different communication styles. Understanding whether a culture uses direct or indirect communication can prevent misunderstandings."}},{"id":"nN4oO5pP6q","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Direct communication cultures (e.g. Germany, Netherlands, USA): people say exactly what they mean. Clarity is valued over politeness."}},{"id":"qQ7rR8sS9t","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'I disagree with your proposal.'","'This is not what we agreed on.'"]}},{"id":"tT0uU1vV2w","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Indirect communication cultures (e.g. Japan, Korea, many Arab countries): people imply meaning and avoid open disagreement. Harmony is prioritised."}},{"id":"wW3xX4yY5z","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["'That could be difficult to implement...' (meaning: no)","'I see...' (meaning: I'm not sure I agree)"]}},{"id":"zA6bB7cC8d","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Key vocabulary: to imply, to hint at, to read between the lines, to be straightforward, to beat around the bush, face-saving"}},{"id":"dD9eE0fF1g","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"At B1 level, you should recognise these styles and adapt your language for different audiences."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: In indirect cultures, people often imply their meaning rather than stating it directly.

items.text: That might be a little challenging to arrange.
This report has several errors that need fixing.
There are perhaps one or two areas we could look at again.
The deadline is tomorrow. No exceptions.
It would be wonderful if we could try to finish soon.

guessItems.hint: To understand the hidden meaning behind what someone says
To avoid getting to the main point directly

pairs.english: In indirect cultures, people often imply their meaning rather than stating it directly.
pairs.russian: В культурах с косвенной коммуникацией люди часто подразумевают своё мнение, не выражая его прямо.

pairs.english: It is important to read between the lines when communicating with people from different backgrounds.
pairs.russian: Важно улавливать скрытый смысл при общении с людьми из разных культурных традиций.

subtopics.title: 3.2 Misunderstandings and How to Resolve Them

content.content: {"time":1700000406000,"blocks":[{"id":"gG2hH3iI4j","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Misunderstandings happen in cross-cultural communication. Knowing how to respond appropriately is a key B1 skill."}},{"id":"jJ5kK6lL7m","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Common causes of misunderstandings:"}},{"id":"mM8nN9oO0p","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["Different expectations about personal space or eye contact","Different meanings of silence or pauses in conversation","Gestures that mean different things in different cultures","Different attitudes to punctuality and deadlines"]}},{"id":"pP1qQ2rR3s","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Useful language for clarifying and resolving misunderstandings:"}},{"id":"sS4tT5uU6v","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["I'm sorry, I'm not sure I understood correctly — did you mean...?","Could you clarify what you meant by...?","I apologise if I gave the wrong impression. What I meant was...","I think there may have been a misunderstanding — let me explain.","In my culture, this gesture/phrase usually means..., but I realise it may be different here."]}},{"id":"vV7wW8xX9y","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"The past perfect is useful for explaining what had happened before a misunderstanding: I hadn't realised that arriving late was considered rude."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: I apologise if I gave the wrong impression. I hadn't realised that this gesture could be considered rude.

content.targetPhrase: I think there may have been a misunderstanding. Could you clarify what you meant?

content.text: I [apologise] if I gave the wrong impression earlier. I [hadn't realised] that refusing food could be seen as rude in your culture. What I [meant] was that I was simply not hungry at the time. In the future, I will try to be more [aware] of cultural differences.

questions.text: Which sentence uses the past perfect correctly to explain a misunderstanding?
options: I didn't realise it was rude until someone told me.
I hadn't realised it was considered rude before he explained.
I don't realise it was rude at the time.
I have not realised it was rude.

questions.text: Which phrase is best for clarifying a misunderstanding politely?
options: Could you clarify what you meant by that?

content.content: {"time":1700000407000,"blocks":[{"id":"yY0zA1bB2c","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"A stereotype is a fixed, oversimplified idea about a particular group of people. Stereotypes can be positive or negative, but both are harmful because they ignore individual differences."}},{"id":"cC3dD4eE5f","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Key vocabulary:"}},{"id":"fF6gG7hH8i","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["prejudice — an unfair negative opinion formed without full knowledge","discrimination — treating people unfairly because of who they are","bias — an unfair preference for or against something","assumption — something you believe without evidence","inclusive — welcoming and respectful of all people"]}},{"id":"iI9jJ0kK1l","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Language for challenging stereotypes:"}},{"id":"lL2mM3nN4o","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["That's a common misconception, but in reality...","While some people may... it's important to remember that individuals vary greatly.","It's not fair to generalise about all [nationality/group] based on...","This stereotype doesn't reflect the diversity within the culture."]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: That's a common misconception, but in reality individuals vary greatly within every culture.

pairs.right: a fixed, oversimplified belief about a group
an unfair negative opinion without full knowledge
treating people unfairly based on who they are
an unfair preference for or against something
believing something without evidence

questions.text: What is the problem with positive stereotypes?
options: They still ignore individual differences and can create unfair expectations.
They help people understand other cultures better.

questions.text: Which phrase best challenges a stereotype politely?
options: That's a common misconception, but in reality individuals vary greatly.

content.content: {"time":1700000408000,"blocks":[{"id":"oO5pP6qQ7r","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Cultural sensitivity means being aware of and respectful towards cultural differences. It is an essential skill in international workplaces, schools, and communities."}},{"id":"rR8sS9tT0u","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Principles of cultural sensitivity:"}},{"id":"uU1vV2wW3x","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["Listen actively — pay full attention without interrupting","Avoid assumptions — don't assume everyone shares your values","Ask respectfully — if unsure, ask politely rather than guessing","Acknowledge differences — recognise that differences exist without judging them","Adapt your behaviour — adjust your communication style when needed"]}},{"id":"xX4yY5zA6b","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Polite questions to learn about someone's culture:"}},{"id":"bB7cC8dD9e","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["Could you tell me a bit about how you celebrate...?","I hope you don't mind me asking — is it customary to...?","I'd love to learn more about your traditions. Could you explain...?"]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: I hope you don't mind me asking — is it customary to remove shoes before entering your home?

tasks.sentence: I hope you don't ___ me asking — is it customary to remove shoes at the door?
Could you tell me a bit ___ how you celebrate this festival?

pairs.english: Cultural sensitivity means being aware of and respectful towards cultural differences.
pairs.russian: Культурная чувствительность означает осознание культурных различий и уважение к ним.

pairs.russian: Важно не делать предположений о чьих-то ценностях на основе их национальности.

lessons.title: Talking About Food and Cultural Meaning

content.content: {"time":1700000409000,"blocks":[{"id":"eE0fF1gG2h","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Food is one of the most powerful expressions of cultural identity. What people eat, how they prepare it, and who they share it with all carry deep cultural meaning."}},{"id":"hH3iI4jJ5k","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Ways food reflects culture:"}},{"id":"kK6lL7mM8n","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["Ingredients reflect the geography and climate of a region","Recipes are passed down through generations as part of heritage","Sharing meals is central to social bonding in many cultures","Certain foods carry religious or spiritual significance","Street food and markets reflect the daily life and economy of a place"]}},{"id":"nN9oO0pP1q","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Describing food culturally:"}},{"id":"qQ2rR3sS4t","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["This dish is traditionally made during...","It has been a staple food in [country] for centuries.","The recipe has been passed down through generations in my family.","It is usually eaten during festivals / religious celebrations / family gatherings."]}},{"id":"tT5uU6vV7w","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Vocabulary: staple food, cuisine, ingredient, recipe, to prepare, to serve, to be associated with, to symbolise"}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: Rice has been a staple food in many Asian cultures for centuries.

Rice has been a [staple food] in many Asian cultures for centuries. The recipe for this dish has been [passed down] through generations in my grandmother's family. It is [traditionally] prepared during the New Year festival and [symbolises] prosperity and good luck.

options: A food that is very expensive
A food that forms the basis of a diet and is eaten regularly
A food only eaten at special celebrations
A foreign food that is recently popular

questions.text: Which phrase means a recipe was taught from parents to children over time?
options: The recipe has been passed down through generations.
The recipe was discovered by accident.

content.content: {"time":1700000410000,"blocks":[{"id":"wW8xX9yY0z","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"In multicultural environments, it is important to understand and respect dietary choices and restrictions. Some are based on religion, others on health or personal values."}},{"id":"zA1bB2cC3d","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Common dietary types:"}},{"id":"dD4eE5fF6g","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["Vegetarian — does not eat meat or fish","Vegan — avoids all animal products including dairy and eggs","Halal — food prepared according to Islamic law","Kosher — food prepared according to Jewish dietary laws","Gluten-free — avoids gluten, often due to coeliac disease","Lactose intolerant — cannot digest dairy products"]}},{"id":"gG7hH8iI9j","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Polite phrases for discussing food restrictions:"}},{"id":"jJ0kK1lL2m","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["I should mention that I'm vegetarian — I hope that's not a problem.","Could you let me know if there are any meat-free options?","Do you happen to know if this dish contains...?","I'm afraid I can't eat... for religious/health reasons."]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.content: {"time":1700000411000,"blocks":[{"id":"mM3nN4oO5p","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Festivals and celebrations are windows into a culture's values, beliefs, and history. At B1 level, you should be able to describe a festival, explain its significance, and compare it with others."}},{"id":"pP6qQ7rR8s","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Famous festivals around the world:"}},{"id":"sS9tT0uU1v","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["Diwali (India) — the festival of lights; celebrates the victory of light over darkness with candles, fireworks, and sweets","Carnival (Brazil) — a lively street festival with music, costumes, and dancing before Lent","Chinese New Year — a two-week celebration with dragon dances, fireworks, and family gatherings","Oktoberfest (Germany) — a traditional Bavarian festival celebrating autumn with food, music, and beer","Eid al-Fitr (Muslim world) — a religious holiday marking the end of Ramadan with prayers, feasting, and gifts"]}},{"id":"vV2wW3xX4y","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Useful language:"}},{"id":"yY5zA6bB7c","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["The festival takes place every year in...","It is celebrated to mark...","One of the most important aspects of the festival is...","People come together to..."]}}],"version":"2.31.4"}

content.text: Diwali is the festival of lights, celebrated to mark the victory of light over darkness.

pairs.right: festival of lights celebrated in India
a colourful street festival in Brazil
celebrated with dragon dances and fireworks
Bavarian autumn festival in Germany
marks the end of Ramadan in Muslim communities

content.text: Diwali [takes place] every year in autumn and is celebrated to [mark] the victory of light over darkness. One of the most important [aspects] of the festival is lighting oil lamps called diyas. Families [come together] to share sweets and watch fireworks.

content.content: {"time":1700000412000,"blocks":[{"id":"cC8dD9eE0f","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Being able to describe your own cultural celebrations in English is an important communication skill. Use a mix of tenses and descriptive language."}},{"id":"fF1gG2hH3i","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Present simple for regular customs: Every year, we decorate our homes with lights and flowers."}},{"id":"iI4jJ5kK6l","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Present perfect for lifelong traditions: My family has always celebrated this festival together."}},{"id":"lL7mM8nN9o","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Past simple for specific memories: Last year, we had a huge gathering with over fifty relatives."}},{"id":"oO0pP1qQ2r","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Descriptive vocabulary for celebrations:"}},{"id":"rR3sS4tT5u","type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["colourful, lively, joyful, solemn, meaningful, spectacular","to decorate, to gather, to feast on, to exchange gifts, to light candles, to perform rituals"]}},{"id":"uU6vV7wW8x","type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Sharing personal experience: For me, the most special part of the celebration is... / What I love most about this festival is... / It always reminds me of..."}}],"version":"2.31.4"}
